newsitem.title: INDIA: India sets deadline for Raytheon airport deal.
newsitem.headline: India sets deadline for Raytheon airport deal.

text.p: India said on Monday it would appoint a new firm to build a $335-million airport in Bangalore if a team involving the U.S. company Raytheon Co and Singapore did not agree to new terms by February 20.

Civil Aviation Minister Chand Mahal Ibrahim told reporters in the southern city of Bangalore that the consortium, which includes Singapore's Changi Airport Authority and India's Tata group, should agree to a build-own-transfer (BOT) arrangement.

The arrangement, which involves a transfer of the airport facilities to Indian authorities after private firms finish building, would mark a change from an agreement under which the consortium proposed a build-own-operate (BOO) scheme.
"If they do not agree at the meeting of February 20 (to the condition), we will give the project to the Airports Authority of India (AAI)," Ibrahim said.

AAI is the state-run body that controls most Indian airports. The project at Bangalore, capital city of Karnataka state, was the first effort to build private facilities since India began economic liberalisation in 1991.
Karnataka's industry minister R.V. Deshpande said he did not support Ibrahim's stand on the airport.
"Definitely, it is sending wrong signals to foreign investors. It is giving us a bad image," he said.

Ibrahim repeated his opposition to another aviation project, a proposed domestic airline involving Singapore Airlines Ltd and the Tata group. The delay on a decision on the issue has raised questions on India's foreign investment policy.
Earlier, Ibrahim had said he opposed the project because Singapore did not allow more than five percent equity for foreigners in its own airline industry.
On Monday, he said competition from the proposed Tata Airline would hurt state-run Indian Airlines Corp.
"I cannot allow 55,000 (Indian Airlines) workers to lose their jobs," he said. He said a tough competitor like Singapore Airlines would add to the losses of Indian Airlines.
Indian Airlines reported a loss of 1.09 billion rupees ($31 million) in 1995/96 (April-March)

Last month, India approved a new aviation policy that permits foreign investors to hold up to 40 percent stakes in a domestic airline. But the policy does not allow foreign airlines directly to hold stakes.
